research_meta.method_note: WebSearch budget was exhausted before any search ran, so no discovery search was possible. Facts come from direct page fetches: English and French Wikipedia (several 2026-27 pages, last edited up to 19 Nov 2026), plus ESPN, Al Jazeera, TheScore, UNFP and Soccerbase pages. BBC, Guardian, L'Equipe, Le Figaro, Reuters and Transfermarkt were blocked or empty in the fetch tool, so those outlets are cited only through Wikipedia references (not read directly). Most Dembele-specific match details (starts, subs, injuries, reasons for absences) could not be confirmed. Nothing was found about interviews, sponsors, business, social-media moments or contract news in the window: that is a research gap, not proof that nothing happened.
gaps: No primary-press article read directly for Aug-Nov 2026 (blocked domains); match facts rest on Wikipedia and Soccerbase.
Reason for Dembele's absences from several PSG matches (e.g. Lille 28 Aug, Le Mans 10 Oct) is undocumented in what was read. Do not speculate on air.
Dembele's involvement in PSG v Villarreal (3 Nov), PSG v Troyes (7 Nov) and France v Italy (12 Nov) is unknown.
Direct YouTube video links could not be verified; viral_moments carry YouTube search links only.
Current look (hair/beard) not verified from recent photos.
No data after about 19 Nov 2026 (Nice away on 21 Nov has not been played).

now.club_or_role: Paris Saint-Germain forward, shirt number 10, under Luis Enrique. Marquinhos is club captain; the English Wikipedia season page lists Hakimi, Vitinha and Dembele as the three vice-captains (French page names the captain only). With France he plays under new coach Zinedine Zidane (in post since July 2026 per English Wikipedia).
now.contract: Signed 12 Aug 2023 for 50.4 million euros; contract runs to June 2028 (English Wikipedia).
season_numbers: 2026-27 club stats as of about 20 Oct 2026 (English Wikipedia squad table; Soccerbase gives the same 4 goals): 10 appearances, 4 goals (Ligue 1: 3 starts + 2 sub apps, 1 goal; Champions League: 3 apps, 3 goals; Super Cup and Trophee des Champions: one sub app each, 0 goals). Not updated for matches after about 20 Oct.
PSG: first in Ligue 1 after 10 matchdays with 23 points (7W 2D 1L, 22 scored, 10 conceded); 4 wins from 4 in the Champions League with 12 points.
Next games: Nice away 21 Nov, Lorient home 28 Nov, Roma home 25 Nov in the Champions League, Intercontinental Cup final 16 Dec in Qatar.
France: won Nations League Group A1 with 13 points; finished fourth at the 2026 World Cup.
what_people_say: He finished 7th in the 2026 Ballon d'Or (418 points), behind teammate Kvaratskhelia (6th), Mbappe (2nd) and winner Harry Kane.
Last season he was Ligue 1 Player of the Year for the second straight year, with 10 goals and 6 assists in 9 league starts (960 minutes), per TheScore.
Mbappe has said Dembele is liked in every dressing room he has been in (French Wikipedia).
now.gaps: No verified information about his form beyond 20 Oct (goal count may have changed), the reasons for several absences, or any contract, business or media news.

quick_context: Dembele came through Rennes, Borussia Dortmund and Barcelona (three La Liga titles) before joining PSG on 12 Aug 2023 for 50.4 million euros.
In 2024-25 he scored 33 goals with 15 assists in 49 games, PSG beat Inter 5-0 in the Champions League final, and he won the Ballon d'Or on 22 Sep 2025.
In 2025-26 he was Ligue 1 Player of the Year again and scored the equalising penalty in the 30 May 2026 Champions League final, which PSG won 4-3 on penalties against Arsenal.

roast_past.angle: Dortmund 2017: sanctioned for missing training without a valid excuse, then moved to Barcelona for 105 million euros plus reported add-ons of about 40 million.
roast_past.joke_seed: Skipped training, got a 105 million raise. Attendance records are overrated.
roast_past.note: Dortmund sanction: French Wikipedia (Aug 2017). Fee: English Wikipedia. French page calls it a missed session, not a strike. Do not call it a strike.

roast_past.angle: Barcelona: listed as one of the club's most-fined players for disciplinary issues (credited to settling down after becoming a father).
roast_past.joke_seed: At Barca he paid more in fines than some players earned in bonuses. At PSG he pays in trophies.
roast_past.note: Fines: English Wikipedia. The earlier 'lifestyle habits criticism' attributed to French Wikipedia was not found and was removed. Keep it to fines.

roast_past.angle: Price tag: 105 million euros for Barcelona in 2017, then sold to PSG for 50.4 million in 2023 after 185 games and 40 goals.
roast_past.joke_seed: About 2.6 million euros of the base fee per Barcelona goal, then the price was cut in half and the goals kept coming.
roast_past.note: 105 / 40 = 2.6 is our own arithmetic on the base fee only. Do not quote it as a record.

roast_past.angle: Rennes coaches worked to cut his individualism and excessive dribbling.
roast_past.joke_seed: Rennes spent years teaching him to pass. He still tries to dribble past the pass.

roast_past.angle: A 2016 post-match interview about which foot he prefers drew attention online; he later said he shoots with the right and dribbles with the left.
roast_past.joke_seed: Asked which foot is his best, he answered like a man who owns both of them.
roast_past.note: Exact quote not verified; do not put words in his mouth.

roast_past.angle: He took the number 10 shirt at PSG after Neymar left in 2023.
roast_past.joke_seed: Inherited Neymar's number, and then actually won the Ballon d'Or in it.
roast_past.note: Number 10 and the 2023 handover: English Wikipedia. Keep the joke on trophies, not on Neymar.

roast_past.angle: Sent off for dissent in October 2019 while at Barcelona.
roast_past.joke_seed: He has been told off by referees in at least two languages.
roast_past.note: Single-source, minor. Optional. The joke about languages is a stretch and can be cut.

roast_now.angle: Defending Ballon d'Or winner finished 7th in 2026 with 418 points, behind teammate Kvaratskhelia (6th) and below Kane, Mbappe, Yamal, Rodri and Messi.
roast_now.joke_seed: From the golden ball to seventh place in 13 months. Even Messi at Inter Miami beat him.
roast_now.note: Ranking: confirmed on two pages. Messi's 5th place is on the same list. Tone: friendly; he still scored 10 league goals in a part-time season.

roast_now.angle: Missed a penalty at Strasbourg on 17 Oct, then set up the equaliser and scored the winner.
roast_now.joke_seed: Missed the penalty, then set up one and scored one. Maybe the penalty was a warm-up.
roast_now.note: Missed penalty and the assist: single source (French Wikipedia). Confirm with a match report before airing. He scored the equalising penalty in the 2026 CL final, so avoid implying he cannot take penalties.

roast_now.angle: Came on after 60 minutes of the Trophee des Champions against ten-man Lens, and PSG still lost 1-0.
roast_now.joke_seed: Lens played most of the game with ten men and still got their first trophy. Thanks for the gift, Paris.
roast_now.note: Lens red card on 39' (before the end of the first half), Lens won 1-0. Dembele's own contribution unknown. Tease the team, not him alone.

roast_now.angle: PSG spent big on wingers and forwards (Torres, Godts, Akliouche) while selling Barcola.
roast_now.joke_seed: Club bought three attackers in August. The Ballon d'Or holder now has colleagues to share the wing with.
roast_now.note: Interpretation. Never link to his injuries or minutes. He is a regular scorer in the Champions League (3 goals in 3 games).

roast_now.angle: France conceded six goals against England in the third-place match and finished fourth at the World Cup, even though he scored.
roast_now.joke_seed: He came off the bench, scored, and France still lost 6-4. At least he did his half of the job.
roast_now.note: France lost 4-6 to England in the third-place match; he came on in the second half and scored France's fourth goal (French Wikipedia; English Wikipedia confirms he scored). Reuters headline confirms 6-4 (not read). The earlier note 'after trailing 4-0' was unsupported and was removed.

roast_now.angle: Won Ligue 1 Player of the Year with only 9 league starts and 960 minutes.
roast_now.joke_seed: Player of the Year on a part-time contract. Efficient. Maybe the other guys should try working less.
roast_now.note: CAUTION: the article ties the low minutes to injuries. Use only as praise or 'efficiency' with no reference to why. Treated as sensitive-adjacent.

roast_now.angle: Reigning European champions started Ligue 1 with two draws and a home loss to Monaco.
roast_now.joke_seed: Champions of Europe opened the league season with a draw, another draw and a home loss. The trophy cabinet needed a month to warm up.
roast_now.note: Do not claim a league position for the first month. The only certain fact is the results. PSG are first now.

praise.angle: Hat-trick in 25 minutes at the World Cup: goals on 7', 20' and 32' against Norway on 26 June 2026; first first-half hat-trick at a World Cup since Oleg Salenko in 1994; third Frenchman with a World Cup hat-trick after Just Fontaine and Mbappe.
Scored the equalising penalty in the Champions League final on 30 May 2026 (1-1 with Arsenal, PSG won 4-3 on penalties).
2024-25 Ballon d'Or season: 33 goals and 15 assists in 49 games, two assists in the 5-0 Champions League final against Inter.
Ligue 1 Player of the Year twice in a row (fifth player ever to do so) and winner of the UNFP Just Fontaine Trophy for best goal on 11 May 2026.
praise.number: 2 awards on one night; back-to-back player award

praise.angle: Slovan Bratislava brace (17', 23') and Manchester City goal (15'): three goals in his first three 2026-27 Champions League games.
Strasbourg on 17 Oct: an assist for the 77' equaliser and the 85' winner in a 3-1 win.
praise.note: Single source for the assist (French Wikipedia, medium confidence). Earlier text said two assists; the Doue assist is unsupported.

no_joke_topics: Injuries and health, including every past hamstring, thigh and calf injury (hamstring tear Feb 2020, tendon rupture and surgery at Euro 2020 in June 2021, hamstring and calf issues in 2025) and any current absence. The reason for his missing matches in Aug-Oct 2026 is unknown, so do not speculate.
His low minutes or number of league starts in 2025-26 as a joke about fitness. Only as a neutral or praise 'efficiency' fact.
Family: his wife and daughter (married 2021, daughter born Sept 2022 per English Wikipedia).
Religion: he is Muslim and observes Ramadan.
The July 2021 hotel video with racist remarks about Japanese technicians: do not joke, do not reference.
Deschamps missing a France match to attend his mother's funeral (June 2026), and the death of Brest coach Eric Roy (June 2026): family and death.
Doping, legal issues, war: nothing found, but do not introduce them.

Rennes coaches worked to reduce his individualism and excessive dribbling; a 2016 interview about his preferred foot drew attention online.
He was sent off for dissent in October 2019.
